clue.text: Word from above is it's not working

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the direction of travel from a higher place to a lower one
second meaning: out of action, as a crashed computer system is said to be

explanation.surface: Sounds like a pronouncement from on high declaring that something has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Word from above' sounds like a divine message, but it simply means a word describing movement from above.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the direction from higher to lower ground, and colloquially describes a broken system or crashed network.

clue.text: Legend one follows still

indicators.note: follows tells us the numeral word is placed after the word for still

parts.note: still, as in 'not finished still', means yet
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A storyteller describing a legend in which one figure trails silently behind another.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a creature of folklore, a legendary beast whose existence is unproven.

clue.text: Commercial music

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short advertisement on radio or television built around a catchy verse
second meaning: a light tinkling sound or simple catchy tune

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue looks like one phrase for pop music; split, each word is a separate meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a brief catchy advertising tune and also a light ringing sound, like bells or coins.

clue.text: Chap tossing one, covering it in fat

indicators.note: covering means the word for fat wraps around the other letters

parts.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking

indicators.note: tossing throws the letters of the number word up so they land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook flipping an item over and smothering it in cooking fat.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled number sits inside the cooking fat to give LEONARD, a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use chap to clue any man's name; this one is a common male first name.

clue.text: Don't eat lean stew — it can make for a hectic life

parts.note: to fast is to go without food

indicators.note: to stew is to cook something slowly into a mush, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Diet advice: skipping a lean stew may lead to a frantic lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like a dish, but it is the signal to rearrange lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Living in the fast lane is the idiom for a busy, pressured, high-speed lifestyle.

clue.text: Communication device on the Mars probe beginning to go wrong

indicators.note: something that goes wrong falls out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: beginning asks for just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of probe

explanation.surface: A news report about a space probe's radio failing on Mars.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone with computing features is a device used for calls, messaging and other contact.

clue.text: Lie about gallery's beauty?

parts.note: Miss is the title of a beauty queen, as in Miss World
the Tate is a group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: Someone telling untruths about a beauty contest winner from an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsy: a beauty queen called Miss Tate, after the London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something incorrectly is to give a false account, which is telling falsehoods about the matter.

clue.text: Way to generate income, when artist is English

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a verb; read as 'to generate income'

parts.note: Claude Monet, the French Impressionist painter
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An artist explaining that being English is how to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn an asset or activity into a source of earnings or revenue is to make money from it.

clue.text: Hairy place to be seen with your hand up

definitions.text: Hairy place to be seen with your hand up

parts.words: Hairy place to be seen with your hand up
parts.note: surface reading: a risky spot where you would be noticed raising your hand, as at an auction
setter's reading: a hairy part of the body, which is exposed when you raise your hand

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hairy' suggests a dangerous situation, but it is literal: a body part with hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow under the shoulder joint, usually hairy, shows when the arm is lifted.

clue.text: Conclusion is imminent, when pawn is lost

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so a letter drops out of the word for imminent

parts.note: pending means about to happen
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess commentator saying the game will soon be over now a pawn has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture is apt: losing a pawn, P, from the word for imminent leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The final part or close of something, such as a story or game, is its finish.

clue.text: It makes us turn up as well

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Something that both creates us and makes us show up too.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic material carries the instructions for building every living body, including humans.

clue.text: Dreadful rain must dampen its bare appeal

definitions.note: loosely, the thing whose bare appeal is meant

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad weather spoils the attraction of going about without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence: dreadful rain dampens the appeal of the answer, whose appeal is being bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is the practice of going nude, so the lifestyle's attraction lies in being unclothed.

clue.text: Empty lake beside a field of grass

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of lake
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dried-up lake next to a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic and crossword-familiar word for a meadow or pasture, open grassland.

clue.text: Pulse that is usually found on the head

definitions.note: a description standing for the noun

parts.note: a bean is a pulse, an edible seed
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A remark that a pulse, as in heartbeat, is usually taken at the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat, but here it is the edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting knitted cap is a hat, worn on top of a person's skull.

clue.text: Smell power emanating from jazz

parts.note: BO is body odour
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A powerful smell drifting out of a jazz club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop, often shortened, is a style of fast, complex jazz music from the 1940s.

clue.text: Snoop shows no interest in loud type leaving vehicle

indicators.note: having no of something means it is missing, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: loud means noisy
i is the standard abbreviation for interest, as in interest rates
the type of person who leaves a vehicle in a space

explanation.surface: A spy who seems uninterested in a noisy person getting out of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shows no interest' sounds like indifference, but it means the loud word loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy parker is a busybody who pries into other people's affairs, just as someone who spies does.

clue.text: Hear about a noble comeback

definitions.note: a noun standing for a verb; read as 'make a comeback'

parts.note: re means about, concerning
taken as written

indicators.note: hear asks us to listen, so the words are matched by sound and not by spelling

parts.note: a peer is a nobleman; said aloud after the other parts it gives the right sound

explanation.surface: Gossip about an aristocrat staging a return to public life.
explanation.walkthrough: Say RE A PEER and you hear the word for coming back into view.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up again after being absent is to return or come back into sight.

clue.text: Criticise weird sect going in for medical procedure

indicators.note: going in says these letters enter the word for criticise

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: weird means strange, so the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Complaining about an odd cult that undergoes hospital treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Positron emission tomography is a hospital scanning technique used for diagnosis, such as of cancer.

clue.text: Held out for longer …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: offered or stretched out, as a hand
second meaning: lasting more time than usual, as a stay or a contract

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs into the next clue for the surface only; the two halves here are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both stretched forth, like an offered hand, and prolonged beyond the normal duration.

clue.text: … and captured job that's secure

indicators.note: something captured is held inside, so the word for job sits within another

parts.note: taken as written
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone held captive in a safe post.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly fixed in place, like a ship held by its heavy weight, means made fast or stable.

clue.text: Congress is a part of stable government

indicators.note: is a part of says the letters form a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A political observation that a national assembly belongs to steady governance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks political, but it means sexual intercourse; LEG-OVER is British slang for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Congress is an old formal word for sexual intercourse, and this is a cheeky British slang term for it.

clue.text: Bachelor leaves dry stag looking for mates

definitions.note: describes the state the noun names

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so that letter goes out of the word that follows

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A single man leaves his stag party, out to find a partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stag' suggests a pre-wedding party for the bachelor, but it is the male deer.
explanation.definitionFit: The rut is the breeding season when male deer roar and fight in pursuit of females.

clue.text: It says you can invite any partner along

definitions.text: It says you can invite any partner along

parts.words: It says you can invite any partner along
parts.note: surface reading: a rule or policy allowing guests to bring partners
setter's reading: the note on a wedding or party invitation permitting an extra guest of your choice

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase written on an invitation is also the name of the companion who comes with you.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase on an invitation means the guest may bring one companion, and also names that companion.

clue.text: Unusual layout of capital city terminus

indicators.note: a layout arranges things, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a terminus is the end of the line, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of city

explanation.surface: A commentator on the odd street plan of a main railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Not typical or characteristic means out of the ordinary, irregular, different from normal.

clue.text: Agree to send back note with charges

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
fees are charges for a service

explanation.surface: Consenting to return a bill along with its fees.
explanation.definitionFit: To see fit is to consider it right or decide to do something, so to consent to it.

clue.text: Smart agent grabs short sleep

indicators.note: grabbing something holds it, so the word for agent closes around the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a nap is a brief sleep

explanation.surface: A well-dressed secret agent catching forty winks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy can describe a stylish, neat appearance, as in a snappy dresser, which is sharp or chic.

clue.text: Zealot is so tasteless, when getting upset by female

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter takes this as the slang naff, tasteless, read here as just its opening two letters

explanation.surface: A fanatic so lacking taste that a woman becomes upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: naff is British slang for tasteless, and it seems its opening letters NA are turned up after F to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealous enthusiast or devotee of a team or star is a fanatic, the origin of the shorter word.

clue.text: Vessel essential to house charred bones

indicators.note: essential means at the core, so only the central letters of the word for charred are taken

parts.note: charred means burnt, and these are its middle letters

explanation.surface: A container needed to hold cremated remains.
explanation.walkthrough: Burnt is the word for charred whose core is wanted; the rest of the clue completes the picture of a container for ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall vase-shaped container, notably one holding the ashes of the cremated, is a receptacle.

clue.text: Exercising our men, so they become really big

indicators.note: exercising works the words hard, putting the letters through their paces in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainer working out the troops so they bulk up.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means huge, of very great size, which is extremely large.

clue.text: Account overdrawn — change limits immediately

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of account
the first and last letters of overdrawn
the first and last letters of change

explanation.surface: A bank warning: your account is in the red, so alter your credit limits now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits' looks like a bank's credit limit, but it applies to each of the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without delay, straight away, this very moment.

clue.text: Lobbyist regularly shows little appreciation for those passed over

definitions.text: little appreciation for those passed over

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A political lobbyist often shows scant gratitude to those overlooked for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' suggests people overlooked, but it means passed away; a short tribute to the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary, abbreviated, is a short published tribute to people who have died.

clue.text: Transition point starts to come under sustained pressure

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A turning point begins to come under prolonged strain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is the point where one state or period gives way to another, as on the cusp of adulthood.

clue.text: Condition of late travellers often captured in photographs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the bloodshot, tired look of passengers on an overnight flight
second meaning: the reddened pupils that a camera flash produces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Late travellers' sounds like the dead, but it means people flying through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both an overnight flight's bleary aftermath and the glowing pupils caused by camera flash.

clue.text: Most nimble shot by father perhaps, getting run out

parts.note: a nip is a small shot of spirits

indicators.note: being run out sends the batter off, so a letter is removed from the word for father

parts.note: Father is the title of a Catholic priest
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricketer, the quickest on the field, run out by a throw from his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Run out is a cricket dismissal, but here it means the letter for run leaves the word for priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means quick and agile, so the superlative is the most agile or speediest.
